title: Could You Spell the Street Name?
prerequisites: Recognise numbers and letter names in English.
observable_outcome: The learner asks for one unclear street name to be spelled, then reads back the house number, street, postcode, and town for confirmation.
learning_objective: Clarify one unclear part of a delivery address and confirm the complete address accurately.

scenario.setting: A parcel-delivery phone call in Reunion.
scenario.prompt: A customer says: Deliver it to 14 Rue des Alizes, 97460 Saint-Paul. The courier clearly hears 14, 97460, and Saint-Paul, but the street name is unclear.
scenario.puzzle: Which address part needs repair, and what should the courier say before reading the address back?
scenario.privacy_note: The delivery name and address are fictional teaching data.

model.clarify: Could you spell the street name, please?
model.confirm: So that's 14 Rue des Alizes, 97460 Saint-Paul, right?
model.neutral_variant: Let me check: 14 Rue des Alizes, 97460 Saint-Paul. Is that correct?

language_focus.grammar: Could you + base verb makes a polite request: Could you spell ...? The readback uses So that's ... , right? or Is that correct? to invite confirmation.
language_focus.meaning: Clarifying targets only the unclear part. Reading back the full address checks that every delivery detail is accurate.
language_focus.appropriateness: Could you ... please? is polite in a service call. A shorter Can you spell that? can also work in a friendly context. Do not assume an unclear street name.
language_focus.address_order: For this French address, keep the house number with the street name, then the five-digit postcode with the town. Address formats differ by country.

choice_activity.prompt: The courier heard 14, 97460, and Saint-Paul. Which part needs clarification?

options.feedback: Correct. The street name is the only unclear part, so ask about that detail.
The courier clearly heard 14. Asking for it again adds work but does not repair the unclear street name.
Saint-Paul was clear. The missing evidence is the street name.

request_activity.prompt: Choose the clearest polite repair question.

options.text: Could you spell the street name, please?
options.feedback: Best. It names the exact missing detail and asks for a useful action.
Polite, but too broad. The number, postcode, and town are already clear.
This shows a problem but does not identify what needs repair. It may sound abrupt in a service call.

slot_activity.prompt: Match each detail to its address slot before reading it back.

feedback.house number: Correct. 14 identifies the building on the street.
feedback.street name: 14 is a number, not the street name.
feedback.postcode and town: 14 is not the postcode or town.

feedback.house number: Rue des Alizes names the street; it is not the building number.
feedback.street name: Correct. Rue des Alizes is the street name.
feedback.postcode and town: This is the street, not the postcode and town.

feedback.house number: 97460 is a postcode, not the house number.
feedback.street name: Saint-Paul is the town; this chunk is not the street name.
feedback.postcode and town: Correct. The five-digit postcode stays with the town.

production_task.scenario: A cafe asks for a delivery to 27 Avenue des Palmiers, 97420 Le Port. You hear the number, postcode, and town, but not the avenue name.
production_task.instruction: Write one clarification question. Then write one complete readback question after the customer spells the avenue name.
acceptable_responses: Could you spell the avenue name, please? So that's 27 Avenue des Palmiers, 97420 Le Port, right?
Can you spell the street name, please? Let me check: 27 Avenue des Palmiers, 97420 Le Port. Is that correct?
production_task.valid_variants: Other clear requests and readbacks can work. Street name and avenue name are both acceptable here.

review_prompt: Tomorrow, explain why a courier might ask Could you spell the street name? before saying So that's ... right?

design.texture: Restrained fibres and speckles generated procedurally.
design.depth: Overlapping pieces use offset navy shadows and visible cream cut edges.

visual.title: Repair one slot, then check the whole label
visual.alt_text: A layered papercut delivery label. An unclear street-name slot leads to a polite spelling request. Number, street, postcode, and town then stack into a complete label before a final confirmation check.
visual.prose: First identify the unclear address slot. Ask only for that missing detail. Place the repaired detail beside the number, postcode, and town. Read back the complete label and invite confirmation.
